assertions.description: The feature itself: the constructor must read a `protocols` member off a dictionary passed as the second argument. A getter proves it was read, with no connection needed — before Chrome 154 the object was coerced to a subprotocol string instead.
assertions.test: (()=>{let read=false;const url=new URL('/public/echo-socket',location.href);url.protocol=url.protocol==='https:'?'wss:':'ws:';try{const s=new WebSocket(url.href,{get protocols(){read=true;return [];}});s.close();}catch(e){}return read;})()

assertions.description: The 2011 form must keep working: a single subprotocol string opens a connection and negotiates it.
So must the sequence form. The server prefers `echo` over `chat`, so offering both must negotiate `echo` — which also confirms the offer really reached the server.
Offering nothing is not an error: the connection opens with an empty protocol. Most sockets do not use one.
assertions.test: (async()=>{const url=new URL('/public/echo-socket',location.href);url.protocol=url.protocol==='https:'?'wss:':'ws:';return await new Promise((res)=>{let s;try{s=new WebSocket(url.href);}catch(e){return res(false);}s.addEventListener('open',()=>{const ok=s.protocol==='';s.close();res(ok);});s.addEventListener('error',()=>res(false));setTimeout(()=>{try{s.close();}catch(e){}res(false);},4000);});})()

assertions.description: A repeated subprotocol is a SyntaxError at construction, before any network activity. This rule predates the feature and must survive it.
